newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma wheat makes progress toward maturation.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma wheat makes progress toward maturation.

text.p: Oklahoma's wheat crop made significant progress toward maturation in above normal temperatures and gusty winds during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said in its weekly crop weather report.
Foliar diseases were increasing in some counties and were reaching threshold levels in some localities, the report said.
Wheat was rated 11 percent very poor, 18 poor, 35 fair, 34 good and two excellent.
The state's wheat acreage was 95 percent headed, behind 99 percent in 1996 and on par with the five-year average.

Corn plantings made significant headway while sorghum plantings fell two weeks behind the five-year average. Corn was 88 percent planted, behind 100 last year and the 96 percent average. Sorghum was eight percent planted, well behind the five-year average of 23 percent.
Soybeans were 88 percent planted, ahead of the five-year average of 74 percent.
Livestock conditions were rated one percent poor, 16 fair, 74 good and nine excellent.
Topsoil moisture was rated six percent short, 85 adequate and nine percent surplus.
